title: 7-Layer Cr-Dielectric Stack with Tight Thickness Bounds
scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count to 7 with tight thickness bounds (15-90nm) will eliminate physics_violation failures while maintaining spectral selectivity through fewer but more precisely controlled interference conditions.
design_principle: Minimal viable stack: fewer layers reduce optimization dimensionality and boundary violation risk. Tight bounds prevent solver from exploring physically unrealistic thicknesses that cause numerical instability.
proposed_topology: exactly 7 finite layers from the incident side: Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr
theory_basis: Admittance locus method for metal-dielectric multilayers
known_risks: May not achieve same performance as 11-layer baseline
execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness optimization for an exactly 7-layer planar stack. Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Cr. Optimize only the physical thickness of each finite layer within the user-declared bounds. Do not optimize material identity or layer count in this route. Optimize a 7-layer planar multilayer stack on Al substrate with material sequence Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Cr/HfO2/SiO2/Cr at normal incidence. All 7 finite layers have independent thickness variables bounded [15, 90] nm. Use L-BFGS-B optimizer with hard post-step clipping enforcing min 15nm and max 90nm. Apply quadratic penalty when total thickness deviates from 400nm target. Evaluate mean absorptance in 400-700nm band and mean reflectance in 700-2000nm band. Initialize with 50nm uniform thickness for all layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Reduced from 15 to 7 layers to eliminate physics_violation failures. Tight 15-90nm bounds per feedback directive. L-BFGS-B with clipping addresses solver_disagreement.
